quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jochen Schmitz: Siemens Healthineers lowered its FY2026 revenue growth outlook from 4.5%-5% to 3.5%-4%, mainly because Diagnostics revenue is not recovering in H2, and raised adjusted EPS guidance to EUR 2.35-EUR 2.45, exactly the roughly EUR 0.15 impact of tariff refunds received in Q3; tax rate close to 23% and financial income net around minus EUR 330 million for FY2026.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue growth 3.5%-4%; adjusted EPS EUR 2.35-EUR 2.45

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bernd Montag: Q3 equipment book-to-bill was 1.27 (about 1.17 excluding value partnerships); CFO Jochen Schmitz: Imaging book-to-bill was well above 1.1 and Precision Therapy stronger still.

CEO Bernd Montag / CFO Jochen Schmitz: Q3 FY2026 growth of the synergetic core was 5%, with Precision Therapy +9% and Imaging about 2.3% on tough comps and EUR 75 million to EUR 80 million of revenue shifted into Q4 because site readiness lagged high DryCool factory output; China was down 10%, EMEA was the growth driver; margin excluding tariff refunds was 15.4% (Imaging 21.6%, Precision Therapy 14.1%, Diagnostics 3% before refunds; refunds added 490 basis points in Imaging and 350 in Precision Therapy). For Q4 they expect Imaging to accelerate into the higher single digits, Precision Therapy to grow in the higher single digits and Diagnostics to decline at a mid-single-digit rate.
quarterly_data.figure: synergetic core +5%; China -10%; margin ex tariff refunds 15.4%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jochen Schmitz: Q3 cash in absolute terms amounted to over EUR 1 billion, with a cash conversion rate of 1.12; net debt fell by around EUR 800 million to around EUR 12 billion and leverage from 3.1 to 2.8 times.

CEO Bernd Montag: two new U.S. value partnerships together amount to several hundred million EUR of equipment order intake - a new 10-year strategic alliance with Cleveland Clinic (multiple imaging and therapeutic technologies plus a jointly developed theranostics cancer treatment program) and a multi-year partnership with Vanderbilt Health (diagnostic imaging and radiation oncology, plus AI uses in radiology).
quarterly_data.figure: several hundred million EUR of equipment order intake

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Bernd Montag: photon-counting CT now accounts for roughly 30% of Siemens Healthineers' CT equipment order volume and its U.S. CT market share has risen to levels it is used to in MRI; DryCool accounts for half of MR units ordered; the radiopharmaceuticals business is growing double digits and surpassing the $1 billion U.S. mark this year, with a first 8X Radiopharmacy in the U.K.; Syngo.CT Coronary Cockpit received FDA approval; Atellica Forte was launched at ADLM with 24 assays with CE-marked capillary claims; a CE-marked NfL assay for multiple sclerosis is under FDA review; a new Varian platform launches at ASTRO.
quarterly_data.figure: photon-counting CT ~30% of CT order volume; radiopharmaceuticals above $1 billion U.S.

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jochen Schmitz: Diagnostics continues to decline on the structural rebasing of the Chinese market (Chinese market volume down about 40% versus two years ago) and the tailing off of legacy platforms; China is now in the 10% or so range of group revenue; Siemens Healthineers has built the expansion of Chinese central bidding for imaging into its 2027 plans and will not base guidance on a China recovery.
quarterly_data.figure: China ~10% of revenue; China diagnostics market volume down ~40% vs two years ago

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jochen Schmitz: supply-chain inflation from memory chips, raw materials and logistics cost around EUR 0.01 of EPS in Q3, with around EUR 0.05 assumed for H2 and an impact expected through 2026 and 2027; tungsten prices peaked at about six times and are now two to three times earlier levels.

CFO Jochen Schmitz on FY2027: the baseline is EUR 2.25 adjusted EPS (FY2026 midpoint without tariff refunds) and he expects growth from it, calling this a prudent assessment; the EUR 400 million tariff impact is to be mitigated by 2028, with 2027 mitigation roughly offsetting supply-chain inflation; tax rate expected to normalize to 24%-26%; financial income net to worsen by a mid- to high double-digit million euro amount; recurring separation costs of about EUR 50 million and no branding fee expected; Varian expected to grow in the high single digits.

CEO Bernd Montag / CFO Jochen Schmitz: the deconsolidation by Siemens AG is expected earliest in April next year, with refinancing preparations and shared-service discussions on track; the new Varian radiation therapy platform launches at ASTRO, with deliveries initially below market demand.
